classification.difficultyReason: Recognise an isosceles triangle from identical squares and combine its angle sum with angles at a point.

content.prompt: The diagram shows two identical squares. Find the size of angle $x$.

spec.description: Two identical tilted squares share one central vertex. Their upper adjacent vertices and lower adjacent vertices are joined, forming an upper and a lower triangle. The upper-left triangle angle is 65°; the lower triangle angle at the shared vertex is x. Construction coordinates remain unprinted. No equal-side ticks or right-angle marks are added.
spec.mathematics: The upper triangle has two equal square sides, so both base angles are 65°. Each square contributes 90° at the common vertex. The lower central angle is x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 65° and x are visible; the upper central angle and solved answer remain hidden.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle opposite $x$ at the shared vertex. The upper triangle is isosceles because its two sides are sides of identical squares, so its base angles are both $65^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}-2(65^{\circ})\\\theta&=50^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Each square contributes a right angle. Angles at a point sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}x+90^{\circ}+90^{\circ}+50^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\x+230^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\x&=130^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
